data.headline: Staged switch to alt supplier; hold price 6 weeks then +3%
data.why: Cocoa at 44-year highs and Ghana arrivals down ~50% raise cost risk on current supply. Plan adds 3 weeks stock now, then shifts to alternative source with only +2% cost exposure vs 30% today. Simulated cash peak $3,705 at week 5; payback by week 5. Price rise delayed to week 6 protects volume while cost bridge builds.
data.watch_out: Alternative supplier untested at scale; if its lead time stretches past 4 weeks or quality slips, stockout risk rises while cash is tied in extra inventory. Rival at $5.90 limits price-pass-through room.
data.recheck_when: Next cocoa futures report or Ghana port arrival update; also week 4 inventory check before price move.
data.cost_line: Cocoa +25% × 30% of your cost is cocoa = your cost +7% (+$0.19 a 100 g dark chocolate bar)

what_happened.text: Cocoa rose above $7,000 a ton in New York for the first time.
Bloomberg reported record cocoa prices hurting chocolate makers such as Nestlé and Hershey.
Cocoa hit an all-time high: $12,567 a tonne in London and $11,878 in New York. By the end of April it was 15% lower.
Prices moved sideways, rallied about 9% by mid-May, then eased after rain in Côte d'Ivoire improved the outlook.

caveats: Cocoa's share of this maker's cost is set at 30%. A UK trade analysis puts cocoa at 30–35% of the production cost of a chocolate bar (mass market, about the 2013/14 season; thegrocer.co.uk/analysis-and-features/cocoa-butter-hikes-add-6p-to-a-chocolate-bar/350125.article). A craft maker's labour and packaging share is larger, so this may overstate it. We found no figure for small bean-to-bar makers.

The series is the world cocoa bean price (Pink Sheet, monthly, $/kg). Makers also buy cocoa butter and powder, which moved differently, and many hedge or buy forward through an importer, so they did not pay the spot price.
Each monthly value is treated as the month's mid-point, with straight lines between them. The monthly average peaked at 9.74 $/kg in April; daily highs were higher.

The model has seen this period. Nemotron Ultra's model card gives a pre-training cutoff of September 2025 and a post-training cutoff of May 2026, so a date in the prompt cannot make it forget. The run only gives it news from before the date, and the leak check looks for hindsight in what it wrote.

“Best plan in hindsight” is the best of about 230 plans on a fixed grid (price, start, end, extra stock), run on the real path. Shoppers react to a sweep plan like they did to the nearest price plan the analysis tested; with none tested, they are neutral.
News pages are read as they are today. Any article that names a date after the as-of date is dropped, but a page edited later could still carry hindsight.

A plan that switches supplier is scored with the share of the price rise that Ultra assumed the alternative supplier would feel (`alt_shock_exposure`). The real price path says nothing about whether another supplier would really have been shielded, so those plans' results rest on that assumption.
